Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational 2026-09-27 04:30..23:59: '\TC Boot Watch' event 107 (launched by time trigger) n=1, at 04:35:01; next launch 2026-09-28 00:05:01. No 322, 140, 141, 142 or 111 event for the task in the span.

Same log, same window: '\TC Process Reaper' 107 n=78 and '\TC Sidecar Watchdog' 107 n=78, first 04:30 last 23:45. Both carry the identical DailyTrigger (Rep=PT15M/P1D, StartWhenAvailable, InteractiveToken, UseUnifiedSchedulingEngine true). TC Boot Watch alone also carries a LogonTrigger.

System log Kernel-Power 42 (sleep): 2026-09-26 22:40:20 and 2026-09-28 00:12:03 only; wake 2026-09-27 02:16:59 (Power-Troubleshooter 1). No sleep covers 04:35..00:05, and other TC tasks (Grocery Daily Capture 0800, Capture Watchdog 1030, Ad Pulls 0700) launched through it.
ops/out/logs/boot-watch-2026-09-27.log: 11 runs 02:17..04:35, every one 'BOOT-WATCH-COMPLETE ... findings=0' then 'run-log: finished ... rc=0'. The job never failed; it was not started.

Re-measure 2026-09-28 11:49: Get-ScheduledTask 'TC Boot Watch' State Ready, LastRunTime 2026-09-28 11:35:01, LastTaskResult 0, NextRunTime 11:50:00; boot-watch-2026-09-28.log 34 runs 00:05..11:35, one gap 00:05..03:43 matching the 00:12 sleep. It no longer reproduces.

items.root_cause: Windows Task Scheduler silently stopped starting TC Boot Watch's 15-minute repetition for the rest of a daily window (04:35 to the next 00:05 StartBoundary, 19.5h) while the box was awake, with no event saying why. The class above the instance: a repetition-based TC task depends on the scheduler keeping a repetition alive inside a P1D window, and nothing in the task definition or the job can notice the scheduler dropping it; only health-heartbeat's age bar can, and it did. The job (ops/boot-watch.ps1) and the heartbeat both behaved correctly. The prior close of this type (2026-09-26-b2f93f) was a different mechanism, a finite trigger window ending as ruled, fixed by planned_end, and that fix held.
items.root_fix_none_because: One occurrence in the 3.5 days since the task was registered, with no scheduler event naming a cause. The only structural difference from two identically-scheduled tasks that ran 78 times through the same span is the extra LogonTrigger, and that is a hypothesis, not a measurement. Re-registering a live task's triggers on one unexplained occurrence would be a guess; the stall is self-limiting (the next daily StartBoundary restarts the repetition) and is detected by the existing heartbeat at the 2h bar. Owned as residual 2026-09-28-37406f with the measurement and the candidate change.
items.prevention_none_because: Not a fix that failed to hold: the prior close (b2f93f, planned_end) is a different task and mechanism and it held; this occurrence's producer (Task Scheduler dropping a repetition) has no measured cause yet, so there is no source change to make, and its recurrence pages through health-heartbeat.

prevention.what: Names where this occurrence's class is produced: the registered trigger set of TC Boot Watch (a LogonTrigger beside the PT15M/P1D CalendarTrigger), read by Windows Task Scheduler.
prevention.exact_change: None shipped in this item (see prevention_none_because). Candidate if residual 2026-09-28-37406f records a second occurrence: split the logon half into its own task definition, or replace the CalendarTrigger repetition with a TimeTrigger of indefinite duration, then re-register through the ops registrar.

Job ran rc=0 every time it was started; healthy again (34 runs today, last 11:35). Not a failed prevention: the prior close b2f93f was a different task (harvest crawl planned end) and that fix held. Cause left open as residual 2026-09-28-37406f.
